_doc: Source-licence boundary policy. One entry per upstream whose tree is NOT uniformly under one licence, naming the directories our redistributable artefact must never reach into. Consumed by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-licence-boundary-guard.py; the guard hardcodes no path, no upstream and no symbol. Add an upstream = one entry here, no script change. THAT LAST SENTENCE WAS FALSE UNTIL 2026-09-11: main() read `key = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else "affine"` and licence-guard.yml calls the guard with no key, so a second entry added here would have been checked by nobody and the gate would have gone on reporting green. With no key the guard now checks EVERY upstream below and returns the worst verdict; case 10 of licence-boundary-guard.test.sh holds it to that with a two-upstream fixture, and goes red against the old guard.
_doc_why: AFFiNE was scoped on 2026-09-09 as 'MIT except packages/backend', and de-clouding was authorised on that basis. It was wrong by one directory: packages/common/native is EE too, and the Android Rust crate statically links it into the APK through Cargo, where no JavaScript-level audit can see it. A boundary described in prose gets read once and misremembered; a boundary described in data gets checked every build.

affine._doc_pinned_revision: Full sha, never the branch name. 'canary' is AFFiNE's default branch and moves; this fleet has already been bitten by a rolling-tag hash race. Bump this deliberately, re-run the guard, re-run the patch series.
affine._doc_restricted_dirs: Verbatim from the root LICENSE: content under these two directories is EE-licensed, everything else is MIT. The EE text forbids copying, distributing and sublicensing — which is what shipping an APK, and what vendoring source into this repo, both are. packages/common/native has NO package.json, so it is invisible to a yarn-workspace audit; it is reachable only through Cargo.
affine._doc_scan_roots: Every crate and source directory that ends up inside the APK. The first two are the Android app and the Rust crate that becomes libaffine_mobile_native.so. The third is the crate affine_mobile_native names as affine_nbstore, and it is NOT under either of the other two: the root Cargo.toml maps affine_nbstore to ./packages/frontend/native/nbstore, and that crate takes affine_common as a plain non-optional dependency. Its parent packages/frontend/native is deliberately NOT a scan root -- that crate is the desktop napi module and is never linked into the APK, so flagging it would report a reach that does not ship and make the guard's verdict mean less.
affine._doc_markers: Literal substrings that betray a reach into a restricted dir across ALL THREE of this app's build systems: a Gradle/Apollo schema path, a Cargo path-dependency crate name, a yarn workspace package name. Two traps are baked in here. (1) Cargo RENAMES the directory to a crate name, so scanning for the directory path alone finds nothing — which is how the 2026-09-09 scoping missed affine_common. (2) The Gradle reach is written as a RELATIVE path — schemaFiles.from("../../../../../backend/server/src/schema.gql") — so a marker of 'packages/backend' matches nothing. Markers are therefore the directory tails, not the repo-root paths. Both traps were found by running the guard, not by reading it: the first draft used repo-root paths and silently reported only 2 of the 3 reaches.

known_reaches._doc: The reaches present in PRISTINE upstream at pinned_revision. The guard reports found-vs-known so a NEW reach introduced by an upstream bump is loud, and so the de-cloud work has an explicit checklist. A de-clouded tree must show ZERO; anything here is a to-do, not an allowance.
known_reaches.packages/frontend/apps/android/App/servi: Apollo codegen reads backend/server/src/schema.gql via a relative path — removed by dropping the :service gradle module
known_reaches.packages/frontend/mobile-native/Cargo.to: affine_common path-dependency on packages/common/native — NOT removed by de-clouding; needs the Rust crate patched
use affine_common::hashcash::Stamp for the cloud-auth proof-of-work — NOT removed by de-clouding
known_reaches.packages/frontend/native/nbstore/Cargo.t: affine_common is a NON-OPTIONAL dependency of affine_nbstore, which affine_mobile_native depends on unconditionally. The feature line napi = ["affine_common/napi"] adds a feature to that dependency, it does not gate it -- only `optional = true` would. So the EE crate stays in the APK's Cargo build graph, and packages/common/native must be present on disk to build at all, even with hashcash gone. This is the reach the 2026-09-09 scoping recorded as absent.
known_reaches.packages/frontend/native/nbstore/src/lib: use affine_common::napi_utils::to_napi_error, behind #[cfg(not(feature = "use-as-lib"))]. The Android build DOES set use-as-lib, so this symbol is compiled out on that path -- the source reach is real, the linked-code reach here is not. Flagged anyway because the guard's job is the source boundary: vendoring the EE directory is the prohibited copy whether or not the optimiser later drops the bytes.

vendoring._doc: How the guard finds a vendored upstream inside THIS repository when it is invoked with --repo. It looks for directories whose shape matches the upstream (any scan root or restricted dir present as a subdirectory) rather than for a configured location, because where the tree lands is the owner's choice and is not decided yet. A guard that only looks where it was told is one that a different directory name walks straight past.
vendoring._doc_prune_dirs: Never descended into, for both the tree walk and the file scan. z_archive holds retired app trees and dist holds generated copies; a hit in either is noise that would train a reader to ignore the guard.

acode._doc: cloud-code (#562): Acode vendored at ac_cloud-code/ as an owned tree. Acode is MIT except ONE plugin directory, which is not a licence text but a payload: src/plugins/proot ships prebuilt libproot*.so (GPL-2.0), libtalloc.so (LGPL-3.0) and three Alpine rootfs images, 21 MB of binaries with no corresponding source. Vendoring them into a public repository or signing them into an APK carries the GPL's source obligation, so #562 pruned the directory and dropped the plugin from package.json (devDependencies + cordova.plugins) and package-lock.json. This entry is what keeps that so: it is the fleet-level licence guard #239 requires of every vendored upstream, and it replaces the per-app tester ac_cloud-code/build.json used to point at, which was never written.
acode.restricted_licence: GPL-2.0 / LGPL-3.0 prebuilt binaries without source (proot plugin)
acode._doc_restricted_dirs: Upstream's own F-Droid flavour (utils/scripts/build.sh) removes exactly this plugin, which is the flavour cloud-code builds. Its presence in our tree is the prohibited copy whether or not the build wires it.
acode._doc_scan_files: The reach in a Cordova app is declared at the tree ROOT, not under a source directory: package.json carries the plugin both as a devDependency path (file:src/plugins/proot) and as a cordova.plugins key, and package-lock.json mirrors it. These sit in no scan root, so they are named as files. A declared file that is absent fails closed (exit 2), like a missing scan root.
acode._doc_scan_roots: utils/scripts/ is the JS that runs at build time (upstream's own build scripts): a plugin re-added there would be a reach too. codemirror-lsp-client/ and src/plugins/system/ carry nothing about proot; they are here as DISCOVERY ANCHORS. The repo-mode walk treats every scan root and restricted dir as an anchor, and a tree is recognised when ANY one of them is present (deliberately, so a truncated checkout fails closed rather than vanishing), so each must be a path that exists in Acode's shape and NOWHERE ELSE in this repository. 'hooks' is not here for exactly that reason: it was tried, matched ac_cloud-chat/app, 0_git/src and six AFFiNE component dirs, and the guard then failed closed on all eight for missing siblings. The restricted dir itself is pruned, so it can never be the anchor that finds the tree.
acode._doc_markers: The two spellings of the reach at the pinned revision, verbatim from upstream package.json: the Cordova plugin id com.foxdebug.acode.rk.exec.proot (as a cordova.plugins key and a package-lock entry) and the path dependency file:src/plugins/proot. Deliberately NOT the bare directory tail plugins/proot: src/plugins/terminal/www/Terminal.js names /main/src/plugins/proot/libs/ as a runtime path string in the terminal's own JS, which is upstream's code about a plugin that is not installed, not a build reach, and a marker that hits it would train readers to ignore the guard.
acode._doc_scan_extensions: Manifests and build-time JS only, as for affine. NOT .sh: utils/scripts/build.sh is upstream's own flavour script and names the plugin id in its `cordova plugin remove` branch, which is the opposite of a reach; scanning it would fail the clean tree on the line that removes the thing.

known_reaches._doc: The reaches present in PRISTINE upstream at pinned_revision. cloud-code's tree must show ZERO: the plugin is pruned and both manifests drop it. Anything listed here re-appearing is a to-do, not an allowance.
known_reaches.package-lock.json: three lock entries for the plugin path — removed with the plugin

vendoring._doc_prune_dirs: As for affine, plus Cordova's two generated trees: platforms/ (the Android project `cordova platform add` writes) and plugins/ (installed plugin copies). Both are gitignored, both are regenerated from package.json, and a hit in either is the manifest's hit reported twice.

_doc_what_this_schema_cannot_express: SOURCE COPYLEFT ONLY, AND CLOUD OFFICE NEEDS SOMETHING ELSE. Every field here describes a directory that must not be VENDORED or NAMED in a source tree. Collabora Online is uniformly MPL-2.0, so it has no such directory and an entry for it would be empty in every field — while the boundary that actually binds Cloud Office is trademark, inside the SIGNED APK: Collabora's logo assets under assets/dist/images, and the values Collabora Office / Collabora Productivity Limited at /org.openoffice.Setup/Product/{ooName,ooVendor} in assets/share/registry/main.xcd. Adding that to this schema would report vendored MPL source as a violation (it is not) and would never scan an artefact (which is the only place it lives). It needs a boundary_kind field and an APK reader first. Written down here rather than left out, because an absent entry and a considered omission look identical in a data file. See a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-office-prebuilt-engine-reuse.md section 12.7.
